context.body: A later writer gives Noah a title Genesis never states and places him inside a chain of judgment-and-rescue examples.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Noah and seven others are preserved while the ancient world is judged; the passage also remembers angels, Sodom, Gomorrah, and Lot.
observations.label: Peter calls Noah a preacher of righteousness: action

observations.body: These examples support the claim that the Lord knows how to deliver the godly and reserve the unrighteous for judgment.
observations.label: Peter calls Noah a preacher of righteousness: response

observations.body: preserved Noah with seven others · preacher of righteousness · deliver · judgment
observations.label: Words in 2 Peter 2:4–10

payload.posture: Read 2 Peter 2:4–10 as warning, faith, and water evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The title “preacher of righteousness” is a later canonical claim; this passage does not supply the content or setting of Noah’s preaching.
payload.title: Peter calls Noah a preacher of righteousness
